name: ad1_extract
description: Write the files and folders of an AccessData AD1 logical image (version 4, unencrypted) out as a tree, each file inflated, hashed (SHA-256) and checked against the MD5 and SHA-1 the image records, with a manifest (ad1_extract.tsv) of what went where and ad1_extract.coverage.json (written as incomplete before the first item). Two statuses, kept apart: processing_status (complete, partial, failed: were all items written) and integrity_status (verified, mismatch, unverified, not_applicable: does what was written match the recorded digests); ok is true only for a complete extraction with no mismatch, while the exit status is 0 for a complete one and for one a budget stopped between items (the files were written and the answer says where it stopped; a mismatch is a finding about the image) and 1 when an item broke or could not be written. Data the tree does not lead to is read to its end under the call's clock, in 1 MiB blocks: non-zero bytes in it, or a read the clock stopped before its end, make the answer partial and the integrity unverified, never complete and verified; unreferenced_data says how much was read and where it stopped, counts the gaps with non-zero bytes or not read to their end, lists the first 20 and keeps every one (at most 100,000) in ad1_extract.gaps.jsonl. Budgets (max_items, max_walk, max_bytes, max_ratio, max_seconds) bound the call; one that is reached stops it, keeps what it wrote, and says so. max_ratio holds the bytes written to max_ratio times the bytes of the image's content read (default 1000, as in archive_extract); past it the call stops and names the ratio. A broken or cut file is kept as <name>.partial under a name no other item of its directory holds, and its row's size and sha256 are of the bytes kept. Extracted files carry the host's timestamps, not the item's recorded ones (the manifest and the catalogue's members.tsv have those, with no zone the image records). Run it as a job (job_run tool=ad1_extract) so the files are sealed into the store and the derived catalogue takes them in turn (an archive or a disk image inside). The catalogue's members.tsv for the image (recipe ad1-items) gives the item numbers. SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with one JSON answer (partial, with interrupted true and the signal, and what was done), exit 128 plus the signal, and the removal of the hidden file it was writing; the program it was running is ended by its pid.

image.description: The AD1 image's first segment (.ad1), under inputs/ or a job's output under store/; its further segments are looked for beside it (x.ad2, ...)

members.description: Items from the catalogue's members.tsv for this image: their locators (ad1:item=<address>, the same in a partial and a whole read) or their numbers (n); a folder takes its subtree. Default: every item

out_dir.description: A new or empty directory for the tree. Default: in a job $OUT/<image name less .ad1> (in a job it must be inside $OUT); called directly, work/<your id>/ad1/<image name less .ad1>

max_items.description: Most items taken in this call (default 5,000,000); past it the call stops and says so

max_walk.description: Most items looked at in this call, taken or not (default 5,000,000); past it the call stops, names the item it stopped at, and does not call an item it never reached absent

max_bytes.description: Most bytes written in this call (default 256 GiB); past it the call stops, keeping the file it was in as a .partial

max_ratio.description: Most bytes written per byte of the image's content read (default 1000, at most 1,000,000, with 1 MiB of slack); past it the call stops, keeps the file it was in as a .partial and names the ratio

max_seconds.description: Wall-clock budget in seconds (default 1500, at most 1700); past it the call stops, keeping the file it was in as a .partial
